introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Two smooth spheres $A$ and $B$ of masses $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $1\ \mathrm{kg}$ respectively, collide when moving with velocities $(\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $(\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ respectively.

Given that the velocity of $A$ just after collision is $(2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Find

questions.enonce_markdown: the velocity of $B$ just after the collision, *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Momentum is conserved in the collision. Let $\mathbf{v}_B$ be the velocity of $B$ afterwards (in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$):

$$
2(\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}) + 1\,(\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}) = 2(2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}) + 1\cdot\mathbf{v}_B.
$$

The left side is $3\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k}$ and $2(2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}) = 4\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$, so

$$
\mathbf{v}_B = (3 - 4)\mathbf{i} + (3 - 2)\mathbf{j} + (3 - 2)\mathbf{k} = (-\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.
$$

questions.enonce_markdown: the angle, in degrees, through which the direction of motion of $B$ is deflected, giving your answer correct to $1$ decimal place, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The deflection is the angle $\theta$ between the velocities of $B$ before, $\mathbf{u}_B = \mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$, and after, $\mathbf{v}_B = -\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$. Use the scalar product:

$$
\mathbf{u}_B\cdot\mathbf{v}_B = (1)(-1) + (5)(1) + (-1)(1) = 3, \qquad |\mathbf{u}_B| = \sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}, \qquad |\mathbf{v}_B| = \sqrt{3}.
$$

$$
\cos\theta = \frac{3}{3\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}} = \frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \theta = \arccos\frac{1}{3} = 70.53^\circ.
$$

The direction of motion of $B$ is deflected through $70.5^\circ$ (1 d.p.).

questions.enonce_markdown: the direction of the line of centres at the instant when the spheres collide, *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The spheres are smooth, so the impulse one exerts on the other acts along the line of centres. The impulse on $A$ equals its change of momentum:

$$
\mathbf{J}_A = 2(\mathbf{v}_A - \mathbf{u}_A) = 2\big[(2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}) - (\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k})\big] = 2(\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}).
$$

(For $B$: $\mathbf{v}_B - \mathbf{u}_B = -2\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k} = -2(\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k})$, the same line, opposite sense, as it must be.)

The line of centres is therefore parallel to $\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$, that is, along the unit vector

$$
\hat{\mathbf{n}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}).
$$

questions.enonce_markdown: the coefficient of restitution between $A$ and $B$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Newton's experimental law applies to the components of velocity along the line of centres. Use $\hat{\mathbf{n}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k})$, the direction of the impulse on $A$ (pointing from $B$ towards $A$).

Before the collision:

$$
\mathbf{u}_A\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} = \frac{1 - 2 - 2}{\sqrt{6}} = -\frac{3}{\sqrt{6}}, \qquad \mathbf{u}_B\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} = \frac{1 + 10 + 1}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{12}{\sqrt{6}}.
$$

After the collision:

$$
\mathbf{v}_A\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} = \frac{2 + 2 - 1}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{6}}, \qquad \mathbf{v}_B\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} = \frac{-1 + 2 - 1}{\sqrt{6}} = 0.
$$

(Check: momentum along $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is $2(-3) + 12 = 6$ before and $2(3) + 0 = 6$ after, multiplied by $\tfrac{1}{\sqrt 6}$.)

Speed of approach $= \dfrac{12}{\sqrt{6}} - \left(-\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}}\right) = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{6}}$; speed of separation $= \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}} - 0 = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}}$.

$$
e = \frac{\text{speed of separation}}{\text{speed of approach}} = \frac{3/\sqrt{6}}{15/\sqrt{6}} = \frac{1}{5}.
$$

The coefficient of restitution is $e = 0.2$.
